close_reason: Fixed: doc says 'ASCII byte slices' → 'byte slices'; clarified that case-folding only applies to ASCII letters, non-ASCII passed through unchanged per RFC 4518 §2 v0.1 scope.
description: normalized_eq (line 637) is documented as 'Compare two ASCII byte slices' but the function receives raw Utf8String bytes from any_to_str_bytes — and Utf8String can contain multi-byte UTF-8 (e.g. 'Ångström'). The doc is false: the function accepts non-ASCII input but silently handles it incorrectly (to_ascii_lowercase() is a no-op for bytes >=128, so UTF-8 multi-byte chars are compared literally). The mismatch between the doc claim and actual input domain will mislead maintainers. Fix: update the doc comment to say 'handles ASCII bytes only; non-ASCII bytes are passed through unchanged' and cross-reference the v0.1 limitation note in names_match.
title: normalized_eq doc says ASCII but accepts UTF-8 bytes
